verdicts.conflict: Federal pre-deployment oversight versus regulatory capture and open-weight verification.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic perspective relies on documented historical precedents in cybersecurity where self-certification regimes protect dominant market incumbents. The safetyist position relies on speculative systemic risks without equivalent concrete evidence of state oversight successfully preventing frontier model failures.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical examples of federal pre-deployment audits successfully stopping catastrophic model failures without creating monopolistic bottlenecks would weaken the skeptic claim.

verdicts.conflict: Medical device analogy versus software distribution realities.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic successfully undercuts the medical device analogy by identifying the unique distribution channels of software weights via GitHub. Software lacks the physical supply chain bottlenecks that allow the Food and Drug Administration to inspect and control high-risk medical implants.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Demonstrating that frontier compute clusters function as an enforceable physical bottleneck equivalent to medical device manufacturing plants would restore the analogy.
